lesson.text: Quick memory: how many degrees make a full turn? (360°.) Today: patterns that fit together with no gaps, and patterns that turn.
A tessellation is a pattern of shapes that fit together with no gaps and no overlaps, like floor tiles or a honeycomb.
Only three regular shapes tessellate on their own, because round every point the angles must make 360°: 6 equilateral triangles fit round a point, and so do 4 squares and 3 regular hexagons.
A regular pentagon's angles are 108°. Three make 324°, leaving a gap, and four would overlap, so pentagons alone leave gaps.
Mix shapes to make semi-regular tessellations: two regular octagons (135° each) and a square (90°) fill a point, because 135 + 135 + 90 = 360.
A pattern has rotational symmetry if it fits onto itself as it turns. Its order is how many times it fits in one full turn, and each turn is 360° ÷ the order.
Worked example: an eight-pointed star fits onto itself 8 times in a turn. So its order is 8, and each turn is 360 ÷ 8 = 45°. M. C. Escher (1898-1972) turned tessellations into birds and fish.
Try it in the world: tile a floor in your world with a tessellation, or design a pattern that turns 4 times round a centre. Next: two-point perspective.

exercises.hint: Its angles must fit exactly round a point.
exercises.explain: 3 regular hexagons fit round a point: 3 × 120 = 360.

exercises.prompt: How many squares meet at each corner point in this tiling?
exercises.hint: Count the squares round one corner.

exercises.prompt: A tessellation has no gaps and no overlaps.
exercises.explain: True: the shapes fit together exactly.

exercises.prompt: What is the order of rotational symmetry of this pattern?
exercises.hint: Count the copies of the hook.
exercises.explain: The hook appears 4 times, so it fits onto itself 4 times in a turn: order 4.

What angle does this pattern turn through to fit onto itself (the smallest turn)?
Regular pentagons tessellate on their own.
exercises.explain: False: 3 make 324 and 4 make 432, so they leave gaps or overlap.

exercises.hint: What must the angles round a point add up to?
exercises.explain: 3 × 120 = 360, so three fill a point with no gap.

exercises.prompt: A regular octagon's angles are 135°. Two octagons meet at a point. How many degrees are left?
Match each regular shape to its angle.
What angle does this pattern turn through to fit onto itself?
A pattern fits onto itself every 40°. What is its order of rotational symmetry?
A square has rotational symmetry of order 4.
exercises.hint: Turn a square a quarter turn at a time.
exercises.explain: True: it fits onto itself after 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°: 4 times.

exercises.prompt: Which set of shapes fills a point exactly?
exercises.hint: Add up the angles: 360° fills a point.

exercises.prompt: What is each angle of a regular 12-sided shape?
exercises.hint: A shape with n sides has angles adding to (n − 2) × 180°.

exercises.prompt: This pattern has rotational symmetry of order 3. Does it have a mirror line?
exercises.hint: Would a mirror flip the flags to point the other way?
choices: no: the flags all turn one way
exercises.explain: No: every flag points the same way round, so a mirror would not match it.
